כ"ש בזה המורכב שיסברו שהוא אתרוג כשר ואפשר דמשום הכי אמר פריש או רמון לרבות' דאפי' בזה גזרי' שמא אתי למיסרך וכ"ש במורכב אלא דמ"מ כיון דאין האיסור ברור הוא לא גזרינן ביה ויש ליטלו כל ז' בלא ברכה כנלע"ד: שוב ראיתי בתשובת רמ"א סי' קכ"ו שכ' מהר"י פדואה זיל קרי ביה רב הוא בארצנו שאין יוצאין בו אפי' ע"י הדחק ונתן בהם סימנים שם הא' כי המורכבים הם חלקים ולאתרוגים בליטות קטנות בכל גופם וגובה להם הב' דמורכב העוקץ בולט ובאתרוג [העוקץ] (האתרוג) שוקע עוד נתן סי' במם שבתוכו:
turei_zahav.en:
Of a Jew. For idolatry of a Jew is not helped by nullification.
From the first day onward. These are the words of Rava in the Gemara, who said on page 31 that a lulav of idolatry, which was used for idolatry, should not be taken, and if one took it he has fulfilled his obligation. The Ran and the Maggid explained that this is on the second day of Yom Tov, when a person fulfills with a borrowed one. This is difficult to me, for there they challenge Rava from the Mishnah that teaches that one from an asherah is invalid, and it answers that it is an asherah of Moshe, etc. According to this, there is no challenge at all, for before this, at the beginning of the chapter, Rava holds like Rabbi Yitzchak bar Nachmani, who said regarding the Mishnah that teaches a stolen one is invalid: they taught this only regarding the first day of Yom Tov, but on the second day of Yom Tov, since one fulfills with a borrowed one, one fulfills with a stolen one. It is stated there: Rava said: actually, on the first day of Yom Tov, etc. If so, here too regarding asherah, it is certainly speaking of the first day of Yom Tov, for they are in the same Mishnah. From the words of the Ran it implies that he did not read "Rava said: actually, on Yom Tov," but rather "Rav Ashi," for he wrote that the Razah rules like Rabbi Yitzchak bar Nachmani because Rav Ashi answered according to him, meaning the answer above, "actually, on the first day of Yom Tov." And the reason it is valid after the first day, even though it is forbidden for benefit, is that mitzvos were not given for benefit. It is written in the Levush: there are those who want to validate those esrogim that come from the orchard called Gertiza. I say that they are invalid by Torah law, for it is known that they are grafted, where a branch from an esrog tree was grafted into a marantz or lemon tree, or the reverse. A transgression of grafting was therefore performed with it. Even though a gentile grafted it, there is one who says in chapter Dalet Misos that even a Noachide is commanded regarding grafting a tree. Since a transgression was performed with it, even though it is permitted for eating it is repulsive to the Most High, similar to a crossbred animal, which, even though it is permitted for eating, is forbidden as an offering because a transgression was performed with it and it is repulsive to the Most High. So too here, so it appears to me, end quote. This is difficult for me. If so, what good is that which Rava said to those merchants who sold hadas, that when you buy myrtle from gentiles, you should not cut it yourselves, but they should cut it and give it to you? What is the reason? Ordinary gentiles are robbers of land, etc., as stated on page 30. Ultimately, according to his words, the gentile performed a transgression and it is repulsive to the Most High, for Noachides were commanded regarding robbery. Furthermore, in siman 11 regarding the law of tzitzis, it says that flax planted for idolatrous worship is valid for tzitzis, for it changed; all the more so here, where there is no greater change than this, that after the grafting was done the esrog grew and became a new entity. Furthermore, there is difficulty from what is written in chapter Merubah, page 78, regarding consecrated animals: "or a sheep" excludes crossbreeds. Why do we need a verse? Let us derive that it is a mitzvah that comes through a transgression, according to his words. Rather, certainly a mitzvah that comes through a transgression does not apply here, for the reason we mentioned. It appears to me to forbid it for another reason. In chapter Merubah there, we say: if it comes to include, why do I need two inclusions? Now that a crossbreed is included, need a resembling one be included? Learn from this that there is more reason to forbid a crossbreed than a resembling one. Here we see that an esrog that resembles another is forbidden, for it is stated on page 36 that one resembling a kushite is invalid. Rashi explained: it grew here and resembles a kushite; it is a resembling one and invalid. If so, all the more so a crossbreed is invalid for an esrog, and this Gertiza is a tree graft, so it is obvious that it is invalid. But there is difficulty: from where do we know the prohibition of crossbreed and resembling one regarding esrog? Regarding consecrated animals, firstborn, and tithe, a verse is needed there in chapter Merubah; if so, from where do we know it regarding esrog? One may say that the Rosh wrote in chapter Lulav HaGazul regarding the question whether if signs of tereifah were born in it, what is its law, that the disqualifications of esrog are essentially only from the words of the Sages, and now that the Rabbis enacted regarding esrog, they enacted similar to Torah law regarding consecrated items. So too the Ran wrote at the beginning of the chapter, that regarding the disqualification of beauty, the verse handed it over to the Sages to determine what is beautiful. According to the Tur, who wrote in siman 648 that it is a Torah doubt, one must say that the disqualifications of esrog are a halachah le-Moshe mi-Sinai. If so, regarding crossbreeding too it is so. However, there is difficulty with this: if a grafted esrog is invalid, why do we say on page 31, if he did not find an esrog he should not bring a pomegranate, nor a quince, nor another item, and it did not say the greater novelty, that he should not bring even a grafted esrog? A similar difficulty appears in the Rosh regarding an invalid esrog, that there are those who are precise and ask why it said quince and pomegranate and not another invalid species. One can reject this, that it mentioned quince and pomegranate as a greater novelty, even though they are beautiful and whole, etc. But this cannot answer regarding a grafted one, for a grafted one is also beautiful and whole. Furthermore, is esrog written in the verse? It is written only "the fruit of a beautiful tree," and we derive esrog from it, as is stated in the Gemara through many derivations. This grafted one has all the virtues that an esrog has. And if it is because something that lacks the virtue of an esrog is mixed into it, why should we not compare it to that in Oso VeEs Beno, page 79, in the sugya of a goat that came upon a female deer, where the Sages there hold that even part sheep is called sheep? Here too, let us say that since it has part of the fruit of a beautiful tree, the mixture of another thing within it should not harm it. As for what I brought from a resembling one, that it is invalid, one can reject this, that a resembling one is different, for it is not beautiful since that is not its normal way. In my humble opinion, on the first day one should certainly not take it, since deficiency invalidates then, for we consider that part of the other species as though it is not present, and it follows that what remains of the esrog portion is deficient. According to this, there is no reason to invalidate it on the other days, for a deficient one is valid then. Nevertheless, there is concern that perhaps the majority is from the part that is not the species of esrog, and there is not the required measure remaining from the esrog portion; and it is forbidden even on the other days. It appears that even to take it without a blessing so that the Torah of esrog not be forgotten is seemingly not proper, for we say in the Gemara: if he did not find an esrog, he should not bring another item. Is that not obvious? One might have said he should bring one so that the Torah of esrog not be forgotten; it teaches us that sometimes ruin may result from it, for he may come to be drawn after it. This is said regarding other species that are not esrog at all; all the more so with this grafted one, where people will think it is a valid esrog. Perhaps for this reason it said quince or pomegranate, as a greater novelty, that even with this we decree lest he come to be drawn after it, and all the more so with a grafted one. Nevertheless, since the prohibition is not clear, we do not decree concerning it, and one should take it all seven days without a blessing, so it appears to me. Later I saw in Responsa Rema, siman 126, that Mahari Padua wrote: go read it to schoolchildren in our country, that we do not fulfill with it even in pressing circumstances. He gave signs for them there. First, the grafted ones are smooth, whereas esrogim have small protrusions over their entire body and height. Second, on a grafted one the stem protrudes, whereas on an esrog the stem is sunken. He gave another sign regarding the membrane inside it.

yad_ephraim.he: ס"ק יז וכ"מ סי' תרמ"ה סעיף ז' כצ"ל:
yad_ephraim.en: Subparagraph 17. And so it appears in siman 645 se'if 7; so it should read.

kaf_hachayyim.he: ג) שם. פסולים בגזול וכו' ואם לוקח לולב גזול הולך וצווח לפני הקב"ה ואומר גזול אני ומה"ש אומרים אוי לו לזה שנעשה סניגורו קטיגורו. א"ר אות א' בשם הרוקח ונעלם ממנו שהוא לשון רז"ל ואתמר בי מדרשא פ' אמור ואפס קצהו בירושלמי פ' לולב הגזול. ברכ"י או' א':
kaf_hachayyim.en: 3) Ibid. They are invalid if stolen, etc. If one takes a stolen lulav, it goes and cries out before the Holy One, blessed is He, and says, ‘I am stolen.’ The ministering angels say: Woe to this person, whose defender has become his accuser. Eliyah Rabbah, sec. 1, in the name of the Rokeach. It escaped his notice that this is the language of our Sages, stated in the beis midrash in Parashas Emor, and part of it appears in the Yerushalmi, chapter Lulav HaGazul. Birkei Yosef, sec. 1:

mechaber.he: גנות הצעירים וכיוצא בהם מבתי שמשיהם מותר ליטול משם לולב או שאר מינים למצוה [ואפי' האילן נטוע לפני ע"א כל זמן שאין עובדין האילן] [רבינו ירוחם נ"ח ח"ג]:
mechaber.en: One is permitted to take a lulav or other of the species for the mitzvah from the gardens or similar things at their places of worship [even if the tree was planted in front of idol worship as long as they have not worshiped the tree) (Rabbeinu Yerucham 8:3)].

baer_heitev.he:
מותר. ומ"מ אם יש אחרים אע"פ שאינם יפים כזו יקח אחרים ס"ח סי' תל"ח לענין ערבה ע"ש. ואתרוג המורכב מלימו"ני ואתרוג פסול ויש ג' סימני' האחד המורכב חלק ולאתרוג בלוטות קטנות בכל גופו וגובה להם. הב' המורכב העוקץ בולט ועוקץ האתרוג שוקע. הג' הוא כי תוך המורכב דהיינו המוץ רחב והמוהל שלו רב והקליפ' התיכונה קצרה ובאתרוג הוא להפך כי הקליפה רחבה והתוך קצר והוא כמעט יבש וסימנים אלו מובהקים תשובת רמ"א סימן קכ"ו ובעולת שבת כתב עוד סי' שהאתרוג הגרעין זקוף לאורך האתרוג ובמורכב הגרעין מושכב לרוחב האתרוג ע"ש ועיין תשובת הב"ח סימן קל"ה דמסופק אם יברך עליו מיום שני ואילך ועיין בתשובת שער אפרים חא"ח:
עובדין. נ"ל דאף אם עובדין לאילן אין פסול אלא באותן פירות שישנן באותו שעה שעובדין אותו אבל מה שגדל אח"כ לא נאסר. ט"ז ע"ש:
baer_heitev.en:
Permitted. Nevertheless, if there are others, even though they are not as beautiful as this one, he should take others. Sefer Chassidim, siman 438, regarding aravah; see there. An esrog grafted from a lemon and an esrog is invalid. There are three signs: first, the grafted one is smooth, while an esrog has small bumps over its whole body and they protrude. Second, on the grafted one the stem protrudes, while the stem of an esrog is sunken. Third, the inside of the grafted one, meaning the pulp, is wide and its juice is abundant, and the middle peel is narrow; with an esrog it is the reverse, for the peel is wide and the inside is narrow and is almost dry. These signs are clear. Responsa Rema, siman 126. In Olas Shabbos he wrote another sign: in an esrog the seed stands upright along the length of the esrog, while in a grafted one the seed lies across the width of the esrog; see there. See Responsa Bach, siman 135, where he is uncertain whether to recite a blessing over it from the second day onward. See also Responsa Shaar Ephraim, Orach Chayim.
They worship. It appears to me that even if they worship the tree, the disqualification applies only to those fruits that exist at the time when they worship it; but what grows afterward is not forbidden. Turei Zahav; see there.

beur_hagra.he:
ס"ד גנות הצעירים כו'. דאין הקדש לע"ג כמ"ש בע"א נ"א ב' ע"ג שהיה לה גינה כו' וע' בי"ד סימן קמ"ב סי"ג דשם פסק שאסו' וכמ"ש שם מ"ד ב' רבה בר עולא אמר גנובתיה מהכא כו' נוי מיהא איכא ובטור שם כ' ב' דעות וס' הראשונה סובר שהן מותרין שאין עובדין אותה ולא לנוי נעשו אלא כעין תקרובת ואינו נאסר כיון שאינו כעין פנים שהנטיעה הוא התקרובת ואין זה כעין פנים וכמ"ש בר"פ ר' ישמעאל שם וכ"כ רי"ו כאן וכ' הטור וי"א דלא גרע מנוי והכי מסתב' וכ"פ בש"ע שם כנ"ל:
ואפילו האילן כו'. כמ"ש שם מ"ח א' איזו אשירה כל כו' רש"א כו'. ואפי' לת"ק אמר שם העמיד תחתיה וניטלה כו' כ"ש שלא היה כלל תחתיה:
beur_hagra.en:
Section 4. The gardens of the youths, etc. For there is no consecration to idolatry, as stated in Avodah Zarah 51b: idolatry that had a garden, etc. See Yoreh De'ah 142:13, where he ruled that it is prohibited, as stated there 44b: Rabbah bar Ulla said, its theft is from here, etc.; at least there is adornment. In the Tur there he wrote two opinions. The first view holds that they are permitted, because they do not worship it, and they were not made for adornment but like an offering; and it is not prohibited since it is not like the service within the Temple, for the planting is the offering, and this is not comparable to the service within. This is as written at the beginning of chapter Rabbi Yishmael there, and Rabbeinu Yerucham wrote similarly here. And the Tur wrote: and some say that it is no less than an adornment, and this is reasonable. So the Shulchan Aruch ruled there, as above.
And even the tree, etc. As stated there 48a: what is an asherah? Any, etc.; Rabbi Shimon says, etc. And even according to the first tanna he said there: if one placed it beneath it and it was removed, etc.; all the more so where it was never beneath it at all.

biur_halacha.he:
גנות הצעירים וכו' - עיין במ"ב במש"כ דהכא מיירי שהגינה לא נדבו מעולם לשם ע"ג [ולהרמ"א שם בסימן קמ"ג ס"ג בהג"ה יהיה עכ"פ מיירי דהגינה אינה עומדת בחצר העכו"ם] וכן הדין של הרמ"א דכתב אפי' האילן הנטוע לפני העכו"ם שרי מיירי כאן דנטעו שמשיהם או הנכרים לצורך שמשיהם לאכול פירותיהן ולא מיירי דנטעו אותן לשם הע"ג הסמוך להן דאי היו נוטעין אותן לשם הע"ג והפירות יהיו שייך למשמשיהן אפילו להרמ"א שם בסימן קמ"ג היה אסור לישראל לקנותו אפילו בכל השנה להיות מהנה לכהניהם. ומיושב בזה מה שהקשו השער המלך בהלכות לולב [והגר"א רמז ג"כ לזה בענינינו] דהשו"ע סותר א"ע דשם ביורה דעה סימן קמ"ב סי"ג באילני סרק הנטוע לפני העכו"ם פסק דבכלל נוי עכו"ם הוא והכא מתיר ליקח מהם למצוה דהכא מיירי היכי דלצורך עצמן נטעוהו וכעין זה מצאתי בלבוש וז"ל גנות של שמשי עכו"ם מותר ליטול מהם לולב או שאר מינים למצוה שהם אינם שמורים שם אלא להנאת עצמן ולא לשם עכו"ם ואפילו האילן נטוע לפני עכו"ם כ"ז שאינם עובדין האילן להנאת עצמן נטעוהו עכ"ל ור"ל דמסתמא אמרינן להנאת עצמן נטעוהו אם לא היכא דידעינן דהנטיעה היה לנוי לע"ג ורק הפירות יהיה שייך לכהניהם דאז נקראו נוי עכו"ם ואסור להנות מהן ואינו יוצא בהן ביום ראשון מן הדין דלא מקרי לכם ואף ביום שני לכתחלה אסור וכנ"ל.
ומצאתי בנהר שלום שהקשה ג"כ קושיא זו מיורה דעה סימן קמ"ב סי"ג ותירץ באופן אחר וג"כ כעין שכתבנו דשם דמיירי באילני סרק שאין בהן פירות אנו צריכין לתלות דמסתמא נטעוהו שיהיה לנוי לע"ז משא"כ הכא דמיירי באילנות שיש בהן פירות יותר טוב לתלות שנטעוהו לצורך פירותיהן וכמו שכתב הלבוש.
עוד נלענ"ד לתרץ באופן אחר קצת דהכא דמיירי בארבעה מינים דאיתא לעיל דצריך העכו"ם לקצוץ אותן בעצמן וא"כ לדעת רי"ו המובא בד"מ הוא בכלל ביטול ונתבטל האיסור של נוי עכו"ם ולא נשאר לנו רק דלגבוה צריך להחמיר לכתחלה ולזה מקילינן ואמרינן דלצורך עצמן נטעוהו משא"כ התם לא מיירי רק לענין עצם הדין אם הוא בכלל נוי עכו"ם ונ"מ דאסור לישראל לקצוץ בעצמו:
למצוה - עיין מ"ב מש"כ בשם הס"ח דמ"מ אם יש אחרים יקח האחרים והנה בפמ"ג כתב דמ"מ י"ל גנות עובדי עכו"ם שבחוץ מותר ליטול אתרוג אף שמיוחד להם עכ"ל ודבריו יהיו שייכים רק לתירוץ הראשון שכתבנו למעלה דהמחבר מיירי אף בעומדין בחצר של הע"ז ורק דלא נדבוהו לשם הע"ג ולזה כתב הפמ"ג דבהצטרף לזה מה שעומדין בחוץ לחצר לא מיירי הס"ח אבל לדעת הרמ"א שם מיירי דינא דידן אף היכא דנדבו הגינה לשם ע"ג ואפ"ה מותר משום דמיירי דעומדין חוץ לחצר ואפ"ה הביא במגן אברהם בשם ס"ח דטוב יותר ליקח אחרים. היוצא לדינא היכא דלא נדבו הגינה לשם ע"ג וגם עומדין מחוץ לחצר העכו"ם אין להקפיד ע"ז:
biur_halacha.en:
The gardens of the youths, etc. See the Mishnah Berurah in what I wrote, that here we are dealing with a case where the garden was never donated for idolatry. According to the Rema there in siman 143:3 in the gloss, it will at least be speaking where the garden does not stand in the courtyard of the idol. Likewise, the Rema's law, where he wrote that even a tree planted before the idol is permitted, speaks here where their attendants or the non-Jews planted it for the needs of their attendants, to eat their fruits, and it is not speaking where they planted them for the nearby idolatry. For if they planted them for the idolatry and the fruits belonged to its attendants, even according to the Rema there in siman 143 it would be prohibited for a Jew to buy it even during the year, since he benefits their priests. This resolves what the Sha'ar HaMelekh in Hilchot Lulav challenged, and the Gra also alluded to this in our matter, that the Shulchan Aruch contradicts itself: there in Yoreh De'ah 142:13, regarding barren trees planted before the idol, he rules that they are included in adornments of idolatry, while here he permits taking from them for the mitzvah. Here he is speaking where they planted it for their own needs. I found something similar in the Levush, who writes: gardens of attendants of idolatry, one may take from them a lulav or other species for the mitzvah, because they are kept there only for their own benefit and not for the idolatry; and even if the tree is planted before the idol, as long as they do not worship the tree, they planted it for their own benefit. End quote. He means that ordinarily we say they planted it for their own benefit, except where we know that the planting was for the adornment of idolatry and only the fruits would belong to their priests; then they are called adornments of idolatry, it is prohibited to benefit from them, and one does not fulfill the obligation with them on the first day by law, because they are not called 'for yourselves,' and even on the second day it is prohibited ab initio, as above.
I found in Nahar Shalom that he also raised this difficulty from Yoreh De'ah 142:13, and answered in another way, also similar to what we wrote: there, where it speaks of barren trees that have no fruit, we must assume that ordinarily they planted them to be an adornment for idolatry. This is not so here, where it speaks of fruit-bearing trees; it is better to assume that they planted them for their fruit, as the Levush wrote.
It further appears to me to answer in a slightly different way: here, where it speaks of the four species, it is stated above that the non-Jew must cut them himself. If so, according to Rabbeinu Yerucham cited in the Darkei Moshe, this is included in nullification, and the prohibition of adornment of idolatry has been nullified. What remains is only that for something used before Heaven one should be stringent ab initio; for this we are lenient and say they planted it for their own needs. There, by contrast, he speaks only regarding the essential law, whether it is included in adornments of idolatry, and the practical difference is that it is prohibited for a Jew to cut it himself.
For the mitzvah. See the Mishnah Berurah, where I wrote in the name of Sefer Chasidim that nevertheless, if there are others he should take the others. The Peri Megadim wrote that nevertheless one can say that in the gardens of idolaters which are outside, it is permitted to take an esrog even if it is designated for them. End quote. His words apply only to the first answer that we wrote above, that the Mechaber is speaking even when they stand in the courtyard of the idolatry, only that they were not donated for the idolatry. Regarding that, the Peri Megadim wrote that when this is combined with the fact that they stand outside the courtyard, the Sefer Chasidim did not speak of such a case. But according to the Rema there, our law is speaking even where they donated the garden for idolatry, and nevertheless it is permitted because we are dealing with where they stand outside the courtyard; yet the Magen Avraham brought in the name of Sefer Chasidim that it is better to take others. The practical conclusion is that where they did not donate the garden for idolatry and they also stand outside the courtyard of the idolaters, one need not be particular about this.

eliyah_rabbah.he: [ד] שלא יקצץ וכו'. ובאתרוג בארץ ישראל הוה ליה טבל שנתמרח ביד ישראל (רבינו בצלאל). אתרוג של ערלה ושל תרומה טמאה של טבל פסול ושל דמאי כשר שאפשר שיפקיר נכסיו ויהיה עני שמותר לו לאכול ודמאי של תרומה ושל מעשר שני בירושלים לא יטול ואם נטל כשר (כלבו). ויתר דינים אלו נתבארו בסימן תרל"ז ס"ג:
eliyah_rabbah.en: [4] That he should not cut, etc. With an esrog in Eretz Yisrael, it becomes tevel whose processing was completed in the hand of a Jew. Rabbeinu Betzalel. An esrog of orlah, of impure terumah, or of tevel is invalid. One of demai is valid, for he can render his property ownerless and become a poor person, who is permitted to eat demai. One of terumah or of maaser sheni in Yerushalayim should not be taken, but if he took it, it is valid. Kol Bo. The rest of these laws were explained in siman 637 se'if 3.

levushei_serad.he: <small>סק"ב</small> מאי פריך גבי אונכרי וכו'. היינו דינא דר"מ כאן שלא יקצץ הישראל בעצמו ולשון הש"ס בזה הובא בט"ז סי' תרס"ד ע"ש:
levushei_serad.en: <small>Subparagraph 2</small> What does it ask regarding gentile merchants, etc.? This is the law of the Rema here, that a Jew should not cut it himself. The language of the Talmud on this is brought in the Turei Zahav, siman 664; see there.

machatzit_hashekel.he:
(ס"ק ד) שלא יקצוץ כו' וה"ל טבל ותלי' בפלוגתא שכ' מ"א בס"ק כ' וגרע מאלו לא היה כ"א חשש גזל דחשש גזל כ' מ"א ס"ק ה' דבדיעבד יצא. אבל בחשש טבל דאפי' בדיעבד לא יצא לחד מ"ד ואפשר לדעת המחבר סעיף ה' טבל אפי' בשאר ימים פסול. משא"כ גזל כשר בשאר ימים לחד מ"ד:
בגיטין דף ל"ח. דכתיב וישב ממנו שבי וע"ש ברשב"א שהאריך ובש"ך סי' שס"ג:
machatzit_hashekel.en:
(Subparagraph 4) That he should not cut, etc. And it would be tevel. This depends on the dispute that the Magen Avraham wrote in subparagraph 20. It is worse than if there were only a concern of robbery, for regarding concern of robbery the Magen Avraham wrote in subparagraph 5 that after the fact he has fulfilled his obligation. But with a concern of tevel, according to one opinion he has not fulfilled his obligation even after the fact. And perhaps according to the view of the Mechaber in se'if 5, tevel is invalid even on the other days, unlike robbery, which is valid on the other days according to one opinion.
In Gittin, page 38. For it is written, "and he took captives from them." See there in the Rashba, who elaborated, and in the Shach, siman 363.

magen_avraham.he: מותר ליטול. ומ"מ אם יש אחרים אף על פי שאינן יפים כזו יקח אחרים (ס"ח תל"ח):
magen_avraham.en: It is permitted to take. Nevertheless, if there are others, even though they are not as beautiful as this one, he should take the others. [Sefer Chasidim 438]

mishnah_berurah.he:
(כה) הצעירים - הוא ענין ממשרתי העכו"ם:
(כו) מותר ליטול משם וכו' - הנה לפי המבואר ביו"ד סימן קמ"ג ס"ג ובש"ך ועט"ז שם אין מותר ליטול מהם כ"א כשהוא בחנם ולא בשכר אפילו אם המעות נוטלין הכהנים לעצמן ולא לעבודת כוכבים ואפשר דשם מיירי שמתחלה נדבו הגינה לשם ע"ז והפירות יהיו שייכים למשמשיה להכי אסור להנות למשמשיה והכא מיירי שהגינה לא נדבו מעולם לשם ע"ג ולדעת רמ"א שם בהג"ה בכל גווני יש להקל אם הגינה אינה עומדת בחצר הע"ז והמעות מגיע רק להכהנים ולא לצרכי ע"ג ע"ש:
(כז) למצוה - ומ"מ אם יש אחרים אע"פ שאינן יפין כזו יקח אחרים [ס"ח] ועיין בבה"ל:
(כח) כל זמן שאין עובדין האילן - אבל משהתחילו לעבדו אותן הלולבין והפירות שנמצאו אז על האילן אסורין לכתחלה לגבוה דמאיס והגידולין שיצאו אח"כ אסורין אף להדיוט כמבואר ביו"ד סימן קמ"ה ס"א וי"א שאם קצץ העכו"ם אח"כ ונתן לישראל שרי מטעם בטול ואף לגבוה שרי ולא מקרי מאיס משום שנשתנה שינוי גדול דבשעת עבודה לא היה האתרוג ולולבין וגדלו אחרי כן:
mishnah_berurah.en:
The youths. This refers to the attendants of the idolaters.
It is permitted to take from there, etc. According to what is explained in Yoreh De'ah 143:3 and in the Shach and Atzei Zahav there, it is permitted to take from them only when it is free and not for payment, even if the priests take the money for themselves and not for idolatry. Perhaps there it is speaking where at the outset they donated the garden for idolatry and the fruits belong to its attendants; therefore it is prohibited to benefit its attendants. Here, however, it speaks where the garden was never donated for idolatry. And according to the Rema there in the gloss, in any case one may be lenient if the garden does not stand in the courtyard of the idolatry and the money goes only to the priests and not for the needs of idolatry; see there.
For the mitzvah. Nevertheless, if there are others, even though they are not as beautiful as this one, he should take others. [Sefer Chasidim] See Biur Halacha.
So long as they do not worship the tree. But once they began to worship it, the lulavim and fruits that were then on the tree are prohibited ab initio for use before Heaven, because they are repulsive; and the growths that emerged afterward are prohibited even to an ordinary person, as explained in Yoreh De'ah 145:1. Some say that if the non-Jew afterward cut it and gave it to a Jew, it is permitted because of nullification, and even for use before Heaven it is permitted and is not called repulsive, because it underwent a great change, for at the time of worship the esrog and lulavim did not exist and grew only afterward.

peri_megadim.he: גנות הצעירים עט״ז ועמ״א אות י״ד בזה יע״ש:
peri_megadim.en: The gardens of the young priests. See the Turei Zahav and the Magen Avraham, paragraph 14, on this; see there.

rabbi_akiva_eiger.he: <small>שם בהג"ה </small>והמודר הנאה מלולבו של חבירו. ע' במחנה אפרים בהלכה זכייה מהפקר סי' ד':
rabbi_akiva_eiger.en: <small>There in the gloss</small> One who is prohibited by vow from benefiting from his fellow's lulav. See Machaneh Ephraim, in Hilchos Zechiyah Min HaHefker, siman 4.

turei_zahav.he:
גנות הצעירים. איני יודע פירושו אבל הוא ענין ממשרתי' ע"א:
כ"ז שאין עובדין לאילן. נ"ל דאף אם עובדין לאילן אין פסול אלא באותן פירות שישנן באותו שעה שעובדין אותו אבל מה שגדל אח"כ לא גרע מפשתן הנטוע שעובדין אותו לענין ציצית כמ"ש קודם לזה שודאי אין לך שינוי גדול מזה:
turei_zahav.en:
(א) The young prostitutes. I don't know it, but it's a matter of what I've done

(ב) There is no work for Ilan. N. D. D. D. If you work for Ilana, there is nothing wrong, but in the same fruits that there is in the same hour that works him, but what grows later is not a bad thing that works him for a celestial matter as before that you certainly have no greater change than this:

yad_ephraim.he: ס"ק יט ובתו' שם הוא סיום הס"ק ואח"כ מציין על מ"ש בהג"ה לאכול ממנו מיום ב' ואילך לצאת כו':
yad_ephraim.en: Subparagraph 19. And in Tosafos there is the end of the subparagraph; afterward he refers to what is written in the gloss, "to eat from it from the second day onward, to fulfill," etc.

kaf_hachayyim.he: ד) לפי הזוה"ק פ' תרומה הוא שלא לברך על האתרוג שלוקחו בחנם דהקלי' יונקים מאותן מצות הבאות בחנם. מל"ח סימן כ"ג אות מ"ג. ודברי הזוה"ק הנז' כבר הבאנו לעיל סימן תנ"ד אות ט"ל קחנו משם. ועוד עי"ש אות מ' ואות מ"א:
kaf_hachayyim.en: 4) According to the holy Zohar, Parashas Terumah, one should not recite a blessing over an esrog that he obtained without payment, for the kelipos derive nourishment from mitzvos that come without payment. Moed LeChol Chai, siman 23, sec. 43. We already cited the words of the holy Zohar mentioned above in siman 454, sec. 39; see there. See also there, secs. 40 and 41:

mechaber.he: כל אלו שאמרנו שהם פסולים מפני מומין שביארנו או מפני גזל וגניבה ביום טוב הראשון בלבד אבל בשאר ימים הכל כשר: הגה ויש פוסלין בגזול כל ז' ימים והכי נהוג אבל שאול יוצא בו [טור והמגיד בשם פוסקים] ומותר ליטול לולב של חבירו בלא דעת חבירו בשאר ימים דניחא ליה לאינש למיעבד מצוה בממוניה והוי כשאול [תה"ד סי' ק' ופסקיו סי' קנ"ט] וחסר כשר בשאר ימים [טור] וניטל פטמתו או עוקצו דינו כחסר וכשר מיום ראשון ואילך [רבינו ירוחם נ"ח ח"ג] מיהו אם נקבוהו עכברים לא יטלנו אף שאר הימים משום מאוס [כל בו] עד שיסיר ניקור העכברים אבל אם היה יבש או מנומר שפסול כל שבעת ימים אף אם חתך היבשות או הנמור פסול כל שבעה הואיל ובא מכח פסול (הגהות אשירי פ"ק לולב הגזול) ומותר לכתחלה להתנות על אתרוג שיהיה כולו ליום ראשון ושאינו בודל ממנו כל בין השמשות של ליל שני ואילך ומותר אז לכתחלה לאכול ממנו מיום שני ואילך ולצאת ידי מצוה עם הנשאר (ב"י בשם הרא"ש) אלא שאין אנו בקיאין בתנאים כדלעיל בס"ס תרל"ח בהג"ה. והפיסול שהוא משום עבודת אלילים או מפני שאותו אתרוג אסור באכילה או מפני שאינם מינם או שהם חסרים השיעור בין ביום טוב ראשון בין בשאר ימים פסול (וחזזית פוסלת כל שבעת הימים) (רבינו ירוחם נ"ח ח"ג ור"ן פרק לולב הגזול) והעושים שני ימים טובים פסולי ראשון נוטלין בשני אבל ברוכי לא מברכינן (ואם יש לחבירו לולב ואתרוג כשר יברך על של חבירו מדעתו) (ד"ע):
mechaber.en: Whenever we said that they were invalid due to defects or because they were stolen or robbed, this only applies on the first day of the holiday, but they are valid on the other days. {Rama: RAMA: Some prohibit the stolen [lulav] for all seven days, and this is the practice. But one can fulfill the obligation with a borrowed [lulav] (Tur and Maggid in the name of the Poskim). It is permitted to take an acquaintance's lulav without permission the other days, because people like when a mitzvah is done with their possessions, and it is considered borrowed (Trumat Hadeshen 100 and his responsa 159). One with part of it missing is valid the rest of the days (Tur). One missing its pitom or the bottom tip is treated like one with part missing and is valid after the first day (Rabbeinu Yerucham 8:3). However, if mice punctured it, it should not be taken even on other days because it is gross (Kol Bo) until the mice bites are removed. However, if it was dry or spotted it is invalid all seven days even if the dry spot or spots are cut off, because it came from something invalid (Hagahot Ashiri ch. "Lulav haGazul"). It is permitted, initially, to stipulate on an etrog that it be just for the first day and that one will not separate from it from twilight of the second day on, and then it is permitted to eat from it on the second day on and to use it to fulfill the mitzvah if enough remains (Beit Yosef quoting the Ros"h), though we are not experts in stipulations as we said above at the end of Siman 638 in the note. If it is invalid because of idolatry, because it is forbidden to eat the etrog, because it is not the right species, or because it is not the right size, it is invalid both on the first day and on the subsequent days (and boils invalidate all seven days (Rabbeinu Yerucham 8:3 and Ra"n ch. "Lulav haGazul").) Those who make two days of Yom Tov can take things that are invalid on the first day and use them on the second day but should not bless on them (and if somebody else has a valid lulav and etrog, they should bless on the other one with permission (his own opinion)).}

baer_heitev.he:
ליטול. אבל אסור ליקח מביתו לבית הכנסת או איפכא עיין סימן י"ד ס"ד. מ"א:
פטמתו. ובמט"מ פוסל כשניטל פטמתו משום הדר ולכן אין להקל בפטמא. מ"א:
שיסיר. עיין ט"ז שהעלה דאפי' אם הסיר המאוס פסול ע"ש:
פוסלת. הט"ז כתב להלכה להקל בחזזית בשאר ימים ע"ש:
מדעתו. פי' שיתן לו במתנה בענין דמהני אפי' ביום ראשון אבל שלא מדעתו הוה כשאול ופסול ביום טוב ראשון. וגם בשני מספק. ט"ז:
baer_heitev.en:
To take. But it is forbidden to take it from his house to the synagogue or the reverse. See siman 14 se'if 4. Magen Avraham.
Its pitom. In Mateh Moshe he invalidates when its pitom was removed because of beauty, and therefore one should not be lenient regarding the pitom. Magen Avraham.
That he should remove. See the Turei Zahav, who concluded that even if he removed the repulsive part, it is invalid; see there.
Invalidates. The Turei Zahav wrote as practical law to be lenient regarding chazazis on the other days; see there.
With his knowledge. This means that he should give it to him as a gift in a manner that is effective even on the first day. But without his knowledge it is like borrowed, and is invalid on the first day of Yom Tov, and also on the second day because of doubt. Turei Zahav.
